input.title: fix: separate stored profile class from current limits
input.body:
## Summary

```text
actual upgrade → session profile class = min(6, level + 1)
                       │ survives damage / new World
                       └→ creator load limits → viewer readout / rejection label

current avatar level ────────────────────────→ creator / selection cap
```

Recover original `6d06e28`: keep the profile's stored class separate from current-level eligibility. Level 3 stores 4; two downgrades retain 4; re-earning level 2 writes 3. GameShell shares one profile-class instance across Worlds without adding it to persisted JSON.

The eligibility/label contract already landed in #81. This slice adds the session owner, upgrade writes and live creator/viewer routing, preserving earlier unlock retention, details cleanup and source input behavior.

## Evidence

- **Before:** After real upgrades/downgrades the fixture reports profile Class 4, but the viewer shows Class 2. The new mock regression fails on that mismatch.
  **After:** Native/mock flows display Class 4 alongside the level-1 creator cap of 2, retain GP-only and source empty-suffix rejections, display Class 3 after re-upgrading, and display Class 2 after a new world's first upgrade.
- Primary ActionScript audit verifies initialization, upgrade-only writes, downgrade/reset behavior, stored readout/label versus current-level caps, and absence from serialization. All 11 original paths are accounted for. The model, World and original four unit tests match the checkpoint byte-for-byte; prior eligibility recovery also matches.
- Formatting, TypeScript, 590 tests / 6,696 assertions and production build passed. All ten affected supplied-SWF/mock browser cases passed without skips: eight profile/readout, unlock-retention save/code/load, eligibility and creator/viewer route cases (1.3m), plus two in-game edit/save/secondary-help cases (54s).
- Native/mock Class 4 / Class 3 captures inspected. No generated data or media changes. Cheat flags, full profile entry/reset routes, exact global event timing and synchronized whole-game parity remain unfinished.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** Two-way

No persisted schema migration; revert the session model and prop routing together.

**Blast Radius:** Profile

Changes upgrade bookkeeping and viewer class readouts/labels; creator and selection caps remain current-level based.

input.body:
## Summary

```text
save identity → exact author/name + ordered part fields
                ├─ category-scoped append
                └─ first-match removal

pane origin → local profile / imported code
               └─ retained through detail transfers, fades and code return
```

Recover the core portion of original `47c9ff4`. IDs, code provenance and tank statistics do not define save identity. Browser persistence callbacks and save-button completion states follow in a separate slice; current UI callers still use the default local pane origin.

Primary bytecode rejects the old checkpoint's general identity-based queue filter: initial incremental loading compares IDs, while a separate local refresh does not. Queue behavior is unchanged here; route-specific recovery remains pending.

## Evidence

- **Before:** The recovered pane-origin regression fails: transferred detail has `undefined` origin instead of imported/code origin.
  **After:** Origin survives detail reparenting and fades; fresh setup changes it deliberately. Async code return preserves imported origin without stale disposal removing new panes.
- Original storage tests cover exact author/name, ordered geometry, ignored IDs/statistics, alias suppression, distinct same-ID designs and first-match removal. Added cross-category deletion isolation and asynchronous origin coverage.
- Storage helper, pane model and code-flow model match original checkpoint bytes. ActionScript and bytecode verify comparator fields and distinguish the two queue-loading paths.
- Formatting, TypeScript, 596 tests / 6,724 assertions, production build and all six affected native/mock browser cases pass (55.7s), without skips. Existing creator/viewer routing, code-entry fades and retained preview lifetimes remain verified.
- Live save artwork, persistence wiring, queue refresh routing, hidden-profile-entry lifecycle and synchronized whole-game parity remain unfinished. No schema, generated-data or media changes.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** Two-way

New helpers and optional pane-construction input; existing runtime callers retain their default.

**Blast Radius:** Viewer

Core save comparison and retained-pane metadata. The live save flow is wired separately.
